Mission Local reported that the State Bar required San Francisco District Attorney Brooke Jenkins to participate in an ethics diversion program over her access to and sharing of a confidential rap sheet. The article called the placement ironic, noting Jenkins had moved away from diversion programs championed by her predecessor, Chesa Boudin. It also argued that her explanation for accessing and sharing the record appeared to be a tacit admission of breaking the law.
